Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(s,t\in\mathbb R\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) gives \(p_x>0\), so conditioning on \(X=x\) is well defined.  The replicate definitions imply
\[
 e^{i(sS_1+tS_2)}=e^{i(s+t)A}e^{isU_1}e^{itU_2}.
\]
The two independence assumptions therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 F_x(s,t)
 &=E_P[e^{i(s+t)A}\mid X=x]E_P[e^{isU_1}]E_P[e^{itU_2}]\\
 &=\left\{\int_{\mathcal A}e^{i(s+t)a}f_x(a)\,da\right\}
       \phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\\
 &=\widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For the marked channel, \(\mathrm{lem{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}implications}\) gives \(|Y|\le B_Y\) almost surely, so all marked expectations are finite.  Error independence allows the bounded mark to remain with the latent variables, whence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_x(s,t)
 &=E_P[Ye^{i(s+t)A}\mid X=x]E_P[e^{isU_1}]E_P[e^{itU_2}]\\
 &=\left\{\int_{\mathcal A}e^{i(s+t)a}
       E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]f_x(a)\,da\right\}
       \phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\\
 &=\widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the definition \(q_x=m_xf_x\) justifies the last equality, and \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\) justifies writing both integrals over \(\mathcal A\).  This proves the two identities.

Let \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M\) induce the same observed-data law, and fix \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) gives \(p_x\ge p_{\min}>0\), so the common observed law determines \(F_x\) and \(G_x\).  The nonemptiness lemma shows that this injectivity assertion concerns an inhabited model rather than an empty quantifier.

For either candidate law and either error coordinate, \(\mathrm{lem{:}moment\text{-}derived\text{-}local\text{-}modulus}\) gives
\[
 |\phi_j(v)|\ge1-|v|M_e^{1/q_e}.
\]
Thus, with
\[
 \nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1},\quad c_*=\frac12,
 \quad
 \delta_0=\min\left\{\frac{\nu_*}{2},\frac{1}{4B_A}\right\}>0,
\]
one has \(|\phi_j(v)|\ge c_*\) on \(|v|\le\nu_*\).  Compact dose support and normalization of the conditional density imply, for \(|w|\le2\delta_0\),
\[
 |\widehat f_x(w)-1|
 \le\int_{\mathcal A}|e^{iwa}-1|f_x(a)\,da
 \le B_A|w|\le\frac12.
\]
Hence \(|\widehat f_x(w)|\ge1/2\).  If \(|u|,|t|\le\delta_0\), the factorization lemma yields
\[
 |F_x(u,t)|
 =|\widehat f_x(u+t)|\,|\phi_1(u)|\,|\phi_2(t)|
 \ge\frac18>0.
\]
This uses only the moment-derived neighborhood, not global nonvanishing.

The same moment lemma gives \(E_P|U_2|<\infty\), while compact support gives \(|A|\le B_A\) almost surely.  Dominated differentiation at \(t=0\) is therefore valid.  Define the observed logarithmic derivative
\[
 D_x(u)=
 \frac{\left.\partial_tF_x(u,t)\right|_{t=0}}{F_x(u,0)},
 \quad |u|\le\delta_0.
\]
Differentiating the factorization gives
\[
 D_x(u)=\frac{\widehat f_x'(u)}{\widehat f_x(u)}
        +\frac{\phi_2'(0)}{\phi_2(0)}.
\]
Characteristic-function normalization gives \(\phi_2(0)=1\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}center\text{-}two}\) gives \(\phi_2'(0)=iE_P[U_2]=0\).  Every candidate consequently satisfies
\[
 \widehat f_x'(u)=D_x(u)\widehat f_x(u),
 \quad \widehat f_x(0)=1,
 \quad |u|\le\delta_0.
\]
For the two candidate laws, \(D_x\) is common.  Their transforms are nonzero on this interval, so
\[
 R_x(u)=\frac{\widehat f_x^{(1)}(u)}{\widehat f_x^{(0)}(u)}
\]
satisfies \(R_x'(u)=0\) and \(R_x(0)=1\).  Therefore
\[
 \widehat f_x^{(1)}(u)=\widehat f_x^{(0)}(u),
 \quad |u|\le\delta_0.
\]
Only \(\phi_2\) was differentiated; no normalization on \(U_1\) was used.

Let \(h=f_x^{(1)}-f_x^{(0)}\).  It is integrable and supported on \(\mathcal A\).  For every \(z\in\mathbb C\), Tonelli's theorem gives
\[
 H(z):=\int_{\mathcal A}e^{iza}h(a)\,da
 =\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(iz)^k}{k!}
       \int_{\mathcal A}a^kh(a)\,da,
\]
because
\[
 \int_{\mathcal A}\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
 \frac{|za|^k}{k!}|h(a)|\,da
 \le e^{|z|B_A}\|h\|_1<\infty.
\]
Thus \(H\) is entire.  It vanishes on a real neighborhood of zero by the preceding local equality.  Every real derivative at zero is therefore zero, and these derivatives equal the complex derivatives of the entire function.  Its Taylor series about zero consequently has every coefficient equal to zero and converges on all of \(\mathbb C\), proving \(H(z)=0\) for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).

At \((u,0)\), the two channel factorizations and local nonvanishing give, for each candidate,
\[
 \widehat q_x(u)=\widehat f_x(u)\frac{G_x(u,0)}{F_x(u,0)},
 \quad |u|\le\delta_0.
\]
The right-hand side is common, so the two marked transforms agree locally.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}implications}\),
\[
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)\quad\text{for almost every }a,
 \quad \|q_x\|_1\le B_Y.
\]
Each \(q_x\) is supported on \(\mathcal A\).  Applying the same entire-function argument to the difference of the marked functions extends the local equality to all complex arguments.

For completeness, equality of the real Fourier transforms implies equality of the functions.  If \(h\) is either signal difference and \(g_\epsilon(v)=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/(2\epsilon)}\), then the Gaussian integral and Fubini's theorem give
\[
 (h*g_\epsilon)(a)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
 e^{-ita}\widehat h(t)e^{-\epsilon t^2/2}\,dt=0.
\]
Translation continuity in \(L^1\) gives
\[
 \|h*g_\epsilon-h\|_1
 \le\int g_\epsilon(v)\|h(\cdot-v)-h\|_1\,dv\longrightarrow0.
\]
Hence \(h=0\) almost everywhere.  Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}f\text{-}sobolev}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}q\text{-}sobolev}\), and \(\beta>1/2\) give unique continuous representatives: Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat h(t)|\,dt
 \le
 \left\{\int(1+t^2)^\beta|\widehat h(t)|^2\,dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \left\{\int(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}<\infty.
\]
Fourier inversion supplies continuity, and continuous functions equal almost everywhere are equal everywhere.  Since \(x\) was arbitrary, the common observed law determines every \(f_x,q_x\), even if either error transform has an open zero set away from zero.

Fix a sufficiently large \(n\).  Conditional on \((X_i)_{i=1}^n\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\) makes observations in each nonempty cell independent with their law conditional on \(X=x\).  Each real and imaginary part of a probability-channel summand lies in \([-1,1]\).  The structural-response implication gives \(|Y|\le B_Y\), so the marked-channel parts lie in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\).

The bounded-variable exponential-moment calculation in \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), applied to real and imaginary parts, gives, when \(n_x>\lambda_n\),
\[
 \Pr\left(
 |\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-F_x(s,t)|>2\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(X_i)_{i=1}^n\right)\le4e^{-\lambda_n},
\]
and
\[
 \Pr\left(
 |\widehat G_{x,n}(s,t)-G_x(s,t)|>2B_Y\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(X_i)_{i=1}^n\right)\le4e^{-\lambda_n}.
\]
If \(n_x\le\lambda_n\), channel boundedness and the empty-cell convention give the defining inequalities deterministically because \(\rho^F_{x,n}=2\) and \(\rho^G_{x,n}=2B_Y\).  A conditional union bound over both channels, all cells, and all grid points gives failure probability at most
\[
 8|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|e^{-\lambda_n}=\frac\alpha6.
\]
Combining this with the mass-region failure probability \(\alpha/3\), and integrating over the labels, proves uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\) that
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})
 \ge1-\frac\alpha3-\frac\alpha6\ge1-\alpha.
\]

On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), apply the outer-spline embedding in every cell and the atomic-grid embedding to both error laws, and put
\[
 \bar\theta_n=
 \bigl((p_x,\widetilde f_{x,n},\widetilde q_{x,n})_{x\in\mathcal X},
       \bar\phi_{1,n},\bar\phi_{2,n}\bigr).
\]
The event places the mass vector in \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\).  At \((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\), both coordinates belong to \(\Gamma_n\).  Characteristic functions have modulus at most one; moreover \(|\widehat f_x(u)|\le1\), and the structural-response implication gives \(|\widehat q_x(u)|\le\|q_x\|_1\le B_Y\).  Uniform approximation on an interval of length \(2B_A\) gives
\[
 |\widehat{\widetilde f}_{x,n}(u)-\widehat f_x(u)|\le2B_Aa_{f,n},
 \quad
 |\widehat{\widetilde q}_{x,n}(u)-\widehat q_x(u)|\le2B_Aa_{q,n}.
\]
The atomic embedding gives
\[
 |\bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)|
 \le2\tau_{e,n}.
\]
Using the factorization lemma and the bias allowances,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat{\widetilde f}_{x,n}(s+t)
   \bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-F_x(s,t)|
 &\le2B_Aa_{f,n}+2\tau_{e,n}\le\delta^F_n,\\
 |\widehat{\widetilde q}_{x,n}(s+t)
   \bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-G_x(s,t)|
 &\le2B_Aa_{q,n}+2B_Y\tau_{e,n}\le\delta^G_n.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The event inequalities and these bounds verify all residual restrictions, while the embedding lemmas verify all deterministic restrictions.  Thus \(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) and
\[
 \|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}.
\]

For the samplewise claims, put \(e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\).  For any \(\theta\in\Theta_{n,alpha}\), the simplex, marked envelope, and \(f_x\ge\kappa/2\) on \(I\) imply
\[
 |\mu_\theta(a)|
 \le\sum_xp_x\left(B_Y+\frac{e_n}{f_x(a)}\right)
 \le B_Y+\frac{2e_n}{\kappa}=B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2.
\]
If the feasible set is nonempty, write \(\ell(a)=\inf_\theta\mu_\theta(a)\) and \(u(a)=\sup_\theta\mu_\theta(a)\).  Then
\[
 \ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le B_Y,
 \quad -B_Y\le u(a)+b_{\mu,n},
 \quad \ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le u(a)+b_{\mu,n}.
\]
Together with \(-B_Y\le B_Y\), these inequalities show that the maximum defining \(L_n(a)\) does not exceed the minimum defining \(U_n(a)\).  Both endpoints lie in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\).  If the feasible set is empty, both are zero.  Hence, for every sample,
\[
 L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\quad(a\in I),
 \quad 0\le W_n\le2B_Y.
\]
This proves every assertion.

Fix \(n\) beyond the stability threshold.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}model\text{-}class\text{-}nonempty}\), the uniform assertions below range over a nonempty model.  At fixed \(n\), every coefficient, weight, and atom vector lives in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.  The signal-sieve constraints give
\[
 \|f\|_{L^1(\mathcal A)}\le1+6B_Aa_{f,n},
\]
and the marked envelope gives
\[
 \|q\|_{L^1(\mathcal A)}
 \le B_Y(1+2B_Aa_{f,n})+2B_A(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}).
\]
Equivalence of norms on each fixed spline space turns these into coefficient bounds.  Every continuum constraint is closed, and their arbitrary intersection is closed.  The error constraints are closed subsets of a product of the compact probability simplex and \([-H_n,H_n]^{M_n}\).  Thus all deterministic constraints form a compact parameter set \(K_n^\star\).  Each density coordinate satisfies \(\inf_{a\in I}f_x(a)\ge\kappa/2\), so \((a,\theta)\mapsto\mu_\theta(a)\) is continuous and finite on \(I\times K_n^\star\).

For a sample \(z\), let \(h_n(z,\theta)\) be the maximum of zero and the positive parts of all mass and channel constraint violations, with deterministic constraints absorbed into \(K_n^\star\).  It is measurable in \(z\), continuous in \(\theta\), and
\[
 \Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)=\{\theta\in K_n^\star:h_n(z,\theta)=0\}.
\]
If \(K_n^\star\) is empty, the prescribed endpoints are zero.  Otherwise choose a countable dense subset \(K_{n,0}^\star\).  Then
\[
 d_n(z):=\inf_{\theta\in K_n^\star}h_n(z,\theta)
 =\inf_{\theta\in K_{n,0}^\star}h_n(z,\theta)
\]
is measurable, and compactness shows that the feasible set is nonempty exactly when \(d_n=0\).  For positive integers \(k\), set
\[
 V_{n,k}^+(z,a)=\sup_{\theta\in K_n^\star}
 \{\mu_\theta(a)-kh_n(z,\theta)\},
 \quad
 V_{n,k}^-(z,a)=\sup_{\theta\in K_n^\star}
 \{-\mu_\theta(a)-kh_n(z,\theta)\}.
\]
Each supremum may be taken over \(K_{n,0}^\star\), hence is jointly measurable.  On \(\{d_n=0\}\), compactness gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_{n,k}^+(z,a)&\downarrow
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\theta(a),\\
 V_{n,k}^-(z,a)&\downarrow
 -\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\theta(a).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, comparison with a feasible point forces a maximizing sequence's violation to be \(O(k^{-1})\); every convergent subsequence has a feasible limit, and feasible points give the reverse inequalities.  The empty-set convention proves joint sample-and-index measurability of the extrema and of \(L_n,U_n\).  Uniform continuity on the compact product \(I\times\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)\) makes the extrema continuous in \(a\), so \(W_n\) is measurable by taking its supremum over a fixed countable dense subset of \(I\).

The stability lemma gives, for every sample,
\[
 L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\quad(a\in I),
 \quad 0\le W_n\le2B_Y.
\]
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\).  On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), that lemma supplies \(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) with
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-\mu(a)|\le b_{\mu,n}.
\]
The structural-response implication gives \(-B_Y\le\mu(a)\le B_Y\).  Feasibility gives
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le\mu(a),
 \quad
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)+b_{\mu,n}\ge\mu(a).
\]
Clipping preserves these inequalities.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\subseteq
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}.
\]
Taking probabilities and using the uniform event bound proves coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\).  Joint measurability, endpoint ordering, and coverage verify \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), while clipping gives \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_P[W_n]\le2B_Y\).  The threshold depends only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class indices.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}sobolev\text{-}spline\text{-}jackson}\), the two Sobolev assumptions, and \(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\), there are order-\(d\) splines \(\widetilde f_{x,n}\) and \(\widetilde q_{x,n}\) such that
\[
 \|\widetilde f_{x,n}-f_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}
 \le C_{\beta,\mathcal A}K_n^{1/2-\beta}\|f_x\|_{H^\beta}
 \le a_{f,n},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde q_{x,n}-q_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}
 \le C_{\beta,\mathcal A}K_n^{1/2-\beta}\|q_x\|_{H^\beta}
 \le a_{q,n}.
\]
Since \(\beta>1/2\) and \(K_n\to\infty\), both allowances vanish; in particular, \(a_{f,n}<\kappa/2\) eventually.

The function \(f_x\) is a nonnegative conditional density, and \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\) gives \(\int_{\mathcal A}f_x=1\).  Approximation and \(\mathrm{ass{:}denominator}\) imply
\[
 \widetilde f_{x,n}(a)\ge-a_{f,n}\quad(a\in\mathcal A),
 \quad
 \widetilde f_{x,n}(a)\ge\kappa-a_{f,n}
 =\max\{\kappa/2,\kappa-a_{f,n}\}\quad(a\in I),
\]
and
\[
 \left|\int_{\mathcal A}\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)\,da-1\right|
 \le2B_Aa_{f,n}.
\]
The structural-response implication gives the representative-qualified bound
\[
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a),\quad a\in\mathbb R.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)|
 &\le |q_x(a)|+a_{q,n}\\
 &\le B_Y\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)+a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n},
 \quad a\in\mathcal A.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(a,b\in\mathcal A\), the triangle inequality, the Jackson bounds, and \(\mathrm{lem{:}sobolev\text{-}modulus\text{-}control}\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)-\widetilde f_{x,n}(b)|
 &\le 2a_{f,n}+\Omega_{R_f}(|a-b|),\\
 |\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)-\widetilde q_{x,n}(b)|
 &\le 2a_{q,n}+\Omega_{R_q}(|a-b|).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Hence all constraints defining \(\mathscr F_n\) and \(\mathscr Q_n(\widetilde f_{x,n})\) hold.

The established ADRF identification theorem gives
\[
 \mu(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)},
 \quad a\in I.
\]
For \(a\in I\), all denominators below are positive and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\frac{\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}
       -\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 &\le
 \frac{|\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)-q_x(a)|}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}
 +\frac{|q_x(a)|\,|\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)-f_x(a)|}
 {f_x(a)\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}\\
 &\le\frac{a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}}{\kappa-a_{f,n}}\\
 &\le2\kappa^{-1}(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The last division uses \(\kappa-a_{f,n}\ge\kappa/2>0\).  Summing with the probability weights \(p_x\), taking the supremum over \(I\), and using the definition of \(b_{\mu,n}\) proves the claim.

By \(\mathrm{lem{:}model\text{-}class\text{-}nonempty}\), both \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathscr K\) are nonempty.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}exact\text{-}class\text{-}compactness}\), \(\mathscr K\) is compact.  Let \(h(z,\vartheta)\) be the maximum of zero and the positive parts of all mass and channel violations defining \(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\).  It is measurable in \(z\), continuous in \(\vartheta\), and
\[
 \Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)=
 \{\vartheta\in\mathscr K:h(z,\vartheta)=0\}.
\]
For a countable dense set \(K_0\subset\mathscr K\),
\[
 d(z):=\inf_{\vartheta\in\mathscr K}h(z,\vartheta)
 =\inf_{\vartheta\in K_0}h(z,\vartheta)
\]
is measurable, and compactness makes the feasible set nonempty exactly when \(d=0\).  On that event define
\[
 V_m^+(z,a)=\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathscr K}
 \{\mu_\vartheta(a)-mh(z,\vartheta)\},
 \quad
 V_m^-(z,a)=\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathscr K}
 \{-\mu_\vartheta(a)-mh(z,\vartheta)\}.
\]
Each supremum may be taken over \(K_0\), so it is jointly measurable.  Compactness gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_m^+(z,a)&\downarrow
 \sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\vartheta(a),\\
 V_m^-(z,a)&\downarrow
 -\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\vartheta(a).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, comparison with a feasible point makes a maximizing sequence's violation \(O(m^{-1})\), and every subsequential limit is feasible.  These facts, the prescribed convention when the feasible set is empty, and clipping prove endpoint measurability.  Target continuity from exact-class compactness makes the extrema continuous in \(a\), hence \(W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\) is measurable by taking the supremum over a countable dense subset of \(I\).

Every \(\vartheta\in\mathscr K\) has \(|q_x/f_x|\le B_Y\) on \(I\), so \(|\mu_\vartheta(a)|\le B_Y\).  If the feasible set is nonempty, its infimum is no larger than its supremum, and clipping by \([-B_Y,B_Y]\) preserves endpoint ordering.  If it is empty, both endpoints are zero.  Therefore, for every sample,
\[
 0\le W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\le2B_Y.
\]

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\).  Its projected tuple
\[
 \vartheta_P=
 \bigl((p_x,f_x,q_x)_{x\in\mathcal X},
       \mathcal L_P(U_1),\mathcal L_P(U_2)\bigr)
\]
belongs to \(\mathscr K\).  Indeed, the mass, Sobolev, denominator, moment, and centering clauses are model conditions.  Compact dose support and the density definition give \(f_x=0\) almost everywhere off \(\mathcal A\), and \(q_x=m_xf_x=0\) almost everywhere there.  The continuous Sobolev representatives are nonnegative for \(f_x\) and vanish off \(\mathcal A\) for both signals, so their supports are contained in \(\mathcal A\); normalization gives \(\int f_x=1\).  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}implications}\) gives \(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\) everywhere for those representatives.  On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), the true mass vector is in \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), and the exact factorization identities turn the event's empirical inequalities into the exact feasible-set restrictions.  Thus
\[
 \mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\subseteq
 \{\vartheta_P\in\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
The ADRF identification theorem gives \(\mu=\mu_{\vartheta_P}\) on \(I\).  Profiling and clipping therefore contain \(\mu\) simultaneously on the confidence event.  The analytic-stability lemma supplies probability at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), proving honesty.

Let \(R_n=\{\min_xn_x\ge np_{\min}/2\}\).  On \(R_n\), an empty feasible set has zero width and a nonempty set has width bounded by \(\omega_n\), so \(W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\mathbf1_{R_n}\le\omega_n\).  On \(R_n^c\), use clipping.  The count bound in \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}]
 \le\omega_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}.
\]
The qualitative exact-grid diameter gives \(\omega_n\to0\), and the exponential term vanishes.  Hence the right-hand side is \(o(1)\), with no asserted explicit rate.

The model-class nonemptiness lemma ensures that the theorem's uniform guarantee is nonvacuous.  All measurability, ordering, clipping, honesty, and coverage assertions follow from \(\mathrm{thm{:}honest\text{-}upper}\).  Let
\[
 \mathcal R_n=\{\min_{x\in\mathcal X}n_x\ge np_{\min}/2\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal R_n\), an empty feasible set gives \(W_n=0\).  If the feasible set is nonempty, put
\[
 \ell(a)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a),
 \quad
 u(a)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a).
\]
Since \(L_n(a)\ge\ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\) and \(U_n(a)\le u(a)+b_{\mu,n}\),
\[
 U_n(a)-L_n(a)\le u(a)-\ell(a)+2b_{\mu,n}.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(I\) and using the finite-sieve diameter gives
\[
 W_n\mathbf1_{\mathcal R_n}\le\widetilde\omega_n+2b_{\mu,n}.
\]
On \(\mathcal R_n^c\), clipping gives \(W_n\le2B_Y\).  The count inequality in \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\) therefore gives, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
 E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \le\widetilde\omega_n+2b_{\mu,n}
   +2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}.
\]
The finite-sieve diameter tends to zero.  Also \(b_{\mu,n}\to0\), because it is a fixed positive linear combination of \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) terms and \(\beta>1/2\); the exponential remainder also vanishes.  Hence the displayed bound is \(o(1)\).  No step supplies a quantitative rate for \(\widetilde\omega_n\).

added_lemmas.statement: Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}primitive\text{-}compatibility}\), both the full causal model \(\mathcal M\) and the exact projected nuisance class \(\mathscr K\) are nonempty.  A common witness may be chosen with uniform stratum masses, density \(g_0\) in every stratum, identically zero potential outcomes, and independent centered error laws that are asymmetric and mutually nonidentical and whose \(q_e\)-moments are at most \(M_e/2\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We first verify that the objects in \(\mathrm{def{:}reference\text{-}bump}\) are well defined.  The function \(\widetilde g_0\) is positive on \((-B_A,B_A)\), bounded, and supported on \(\mathcal A=[-B_A,B_A]\).  Hence
\[
 0<\int_{\mathbb R}\widetilde g_0(v)\,dv<\infty,
\]
so \(g_0\) is a nonnegative probability density supported on \(\mathcal A\).  Repeated differentiation on \((-B_A,B_A)\) expresses every derivative of \(\widetilde g_0\) as a finite sum of a rational function of \(B_A^2-a^2\) multiplied by \(\exp\{-1/(B_A^2-a^2)\}\).  Since \(x^{-m}e^{-1/x}\to0\) as \(x\downarrow0\) for every integer \(m\ge0\), all one-sided derivatives vanish at \(\pm B_A\).  Thus \(g_0\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\).  For an integer \(m>\beta+1/2\), integration by parts gives \(|\widehat g_0(t)|\le C_m(1+|t|)^{-m}\), so
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^\beta|\widehat g_0(t)|^2\,dt<\infty.
\]
Consequently \(R_{f,0}=\|g_0\|_{H^\beta}<\infty\).  The function \(g_0\) is continuous and strictly positive on \(\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)\).  Because \(I\) is compact and contained in that interior by \(\mathrm{ass{:}primitive\text{-}compatibility}\), continuity and compactness give
\[
 \kappa_0=\min_{a\in I}g_0(a)>0.
\]

We now construct the full law.  Let \(X\) be uniform on the nonempty finite set \(\mathcal X\).  Conditional on any \(X=x\), let \(A\) have density \(g_0\); equivalently, choose \(A\) independent of \(X\) with that density.  Take \(\mathcal V\) to be a one-point standard Borel space, let \(V\) be its constant random element, and define the jointly measurable map
\[
 h(a,x,V)=0,
 \quad Y(a)=0\quad(a\in\mathcal A),
 \quad Y=0,
\]
and take the displayed equalities on the whole sample space.  Put
\[
 C_e=\max\left\{\frac{3+3^{q_e}}4,
                         \frac{2+2^{q_e}}3\right\},
 \quad
 \delta=\left(\frac{M_e}{2C_e}\right)^{1/q_e}>0.
\]
Independently of \((A,X,V,Y(\cdot),Y)\) and independently of one another, choose
\[
 P(U_1=-\delta)=\frac34,\quad P(U_1=3\delta)=\frac14,
\]
and
\[
 P(U_2=-\delta)=\frac23,\quad P(U_2=2\delta)=\frac13.
\]
Finally set \(S_j=A+U_j\), \(j\in\{1,2\}\).  The two error means are
\[
 E[U_1]=-\frac34\delta+\frac14(3\delta)=0,
 \quad
 E[U_2]=-\frac23\delta+\frac13(2\delta)=0.
\]
Their absolute \(q_e\)-moments obey
\[
 E|U_1|^{q_e}=\frac{3+3^{q_e}}4\delta^{q_e}
 \le C_e\delta^{q_e}=\frac{M_e}{2},
\]
and
\[
 E|U_2|^{q_e}=\frac{2+2^{q_e}}3\delta^{q_e}
 \le C_e\delta^{q_e}=\frac{M_e}{2}.
\]
Each error law is asymmetric: a symmetric two-point law must put equal mass on its two support points, whereas the displayed masses are unequal.  They are mutually nonidentical because their support-and-mass pairs differ.  Product construction gives both error-coordinate independence and independence of the errors from all latent and outcome variables.  In particular, the location normalization for \(U_2\) and the common error-moment bound hold.

It remains to check every retained member property of \(\mathcal M\).  Uniformity and primitive compatibility give
\[
 p_x=|\mathcal X|^{-1}\ge p_{\min}>0.
\]
For every \(x\),
\[
 f_x=g_0,\quad m_x=0,\quad q_x=m_xf_x=0.
\]
Thus \(P(A\in\mathcal A)=1\), \(\|f_x\|_{H^\beta}=R_{f,0}\le R_f\), \(\|q_x\|_{H^\beta}=0\le R_q\), and
\[
 \inf_{a\in I}f_x(a)=\kappa_0\ge\kappa.
\]
The response equation holds on one common probability-one event, \(V\perp A\mid X\), consistency holds because \(Y=Y(A)=0\), and \(a\mapsto E[Y(a)\mid X=x]=0\) is continuous on \(I\).  Hence the constructed full-data law satisfies every retained item in \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\), proving \(\mathcal M\ne\varnothing\).

Project this law to
\[
 \vartheta_0=
 \bigl((|\mathcal X|^{-1},g_0,0)_{x\in\mathcal X},
       \mathcal L(U_1),\mathcal L(U_2)\bigr).
\]
The preceding calculations verify the mass, density, support, Sobolev, overlap, moment, and centering clauses in \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}projected\text{-}class}\); moreover \(|q_x|=0\le B_Yg_0\).  Therefore \(\vartheta_0\in\mathscr K\), so \(\mathscr K\ne\varnothing\) as well.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the structural response representation implies \(A\perp Y(a)\mid X\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).  On one event of probability one,
\[
 \sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|Y(a)|\le B_Y,
\]
and consistency consequently gives \(|Y|\le B_Y\) almost surely.  For every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\), and the inequality holds for every \(a\in\mathbb R\) when \(f_x,q_x\) are taken to be their continuous Sobolev representatives.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\), there are \(V\), \(h\), and one event \(\Omega_0\) with \(P(\Omega_0)=1\) such that \(V\perp A\mid X\), \(h\) takes values in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\), and
\[
 Y(a,\omega)=h(a,X(\omega),V(\omega))
 \quad\text{for every }a\in\mathcal A,
 \quad\omega\in\Omega_0.
\]
Fix \(a\in\mathcal A\).  For bounded Borel functions \(r\) and \(s\), conditional independence of \(A\) and \(V\) given \(X\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P[r(A)s(Y(a))\mid X]
 &=E_P[r(A)s\{h(a,X,V)\}\mid X]\\
 &=E_P[r(A)\mid X]E_P[s\{h(a,X,V)\}\mid X]\\
 &=E_P[r(A)\mid X]E_P[s(Y(a))\mid X]
 \end{aligned}
\]
almost surely.  This is the bounded-test-function characterization of \(A\perp Y(a)\mid X\), proving the first assertion for each \(a\).

Because the same event \(\Omega_0\) works for all doses and the range of \(h\) is \([-B_Y,B_Y]\),
\[
 \sup_{a\in\mathcal A}|Y(a,\omega)|\le B_Y,
 \quad \omega\in\Omega_0.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\) gives \(A\in\mathcal A\) almost surely, and \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) then gives \(|Y|=|Y(A)|\le B_Y\) almost surely.

Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) gives \(p_x>0\), so the conditional law is well defined.  Conditional Jensen's inequality and the observed-outcome bound yield
\[
 |m_x(a)|=|E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]|
 \le E_P[|Y|\mid A=a,X=x]\le B_Y
\]
for \(f_x(a)\,da\)-almost every \(a\).  Since \(q_x=m_xf_x\), it follows that
\[
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\); on the set where \(f_x=0\), the defining identity also gives \(q_x=0\) almost everywhere.

Finally, \(\mathrm{ass{:}f\text{-}sobolev}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}q\text{-}sobolev}\), and \(\beta>1/2\) give continuous representatives of \(f_x\) and \(q_x\).  The continuous representative of the density is nonnegative everywhere, because a negative value would persist on an interval and contradict nonnegativity almost everywhere.  If \(|q_x(a_0)|>B_Yf_x(a_0)\) at some \(a_0\), continuity would make the same strict inequality hold on an interval of positive Lebesgue measure, contradicting the almost-everywhere inequality.  Thus \(|q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)\) everywhere for these representatives.  No pointwise assertion about an arbitrary version of \(m_x\) has been made.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
The set \(\mathcal X\) is nonempty and finite, \(I\) is a nondegenerate compact interval contained in \(\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)\), and the fixed indices satisfy
\[
 B_A>0,\quad \beta>\frac12,\quad q_e>1,\quad
 M_e>0,\quad R_q>0,\quad B_Y\ge1,
\]
and
\[
 0<p_{\min}\le |\mathcal X|^{-1},\quad
 R_f\ge R_{f,0},\quad 0<\kappa\le\kappa_0.
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: Without compatibility between support, Sobolev radius, overlap, and stratum mass, the model could be empty and all uniform inference statements could be vacuous.
proposed_assumptions.standard_or_novel: novel: This fixed-index compatibility condition is exactly what makes the declared quantitative class contain the explicit reference law; it adds no estimator-side requirement.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: It only certifies that the fixed model indices admit a law; it asserts no identification, inverse stability, coverage, rate, or lower-bound construction.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(\widetilde g_0\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The inhabited-model witness needs one explicitly fixed smooth density supported on the dose interval.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(g_0\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: This names the common conditional dose density in the explicit nonempty-model witness.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(R_{f,0}\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The primitive radii must be compatible with the concrete reference density.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(\kappa_0\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The overlap index must be compatible with an explicit density on the target interval.

proposed.name: reference bump density
proposed.construction:
For \(a\in\mathbb R\), let
\[
 \widetilde g_0(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 \exp\{-1/(B_A^2-a^2)\},& |a|<B_A,\\
 0,& |a|\ge B_A,
 \end{cases}
 \quad
 g_0(a)=\frac{\widetilde g_0(a)}
 {\int_{\mathbb R}\widetilde g_0(v)\,dv}.
\]
Define
\[
 R_{f,0}=\|g_0\|_{H^\beta(\mathbb R)},
 \quad
 \kappa_0=\min_{a\in I}g_0(a).
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the explicit smooth positive density used to certify that the fixed model class is inhabited.
Conditional unconfoundedness is proved from the retained structural response surface and is therefore unnecessary as a primitive model restriction.

The common-event structural response surface already takes values in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\); the new structural-implication lemma derives both schedule and observed-outcome boundedness, so a separate primitive bound is unnecessary.

proposed.name: \(\mathcal M\)
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P:P\text{ obeys every condition listed in }\mathrm{by\_member\_properties}\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The class now includes the fixed-index compatibility needed for an explicit witness and removes the two conditions derived by the structural-response implication lemma.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(x\in\mathcal X\), and all real \(s,t\), \(F_x(s,t)=\widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\) and \(G_x(s,t)=\widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\).
proposed.justification: This is the observable two-channel factorization on which injectivity and inference rest.
proposed.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy analyze only the first identity; the marked identity is absent from their model.
proposed.consumer: The empirical characteristic-function confidence set uses these residual equations jointly.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Marked-channel integrability now follows from the proved structural-response implications rather than a redundant primitive bounded-outcome assumption.

proposed.statement: The map \(P\mapsto P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is injective for \(\{(f_x,q_x):x\in\mathcal X\}\) over \(\mathcal M\). On a common neighborhood of zero, \(\left.\partial_t\log F_x(u,t)\right|_{t=0}=\widehat f_x'(u)/\widehat f_x(u)+\phi_2'(0)=\widehat f_x'(u)/\widehat f_x(u)\), because \(\phi_2(0)=1\) and \(\phi_2'(0)=iE_P[U_2]=0\). Together with \(\widehat f_x(0)=1\), this derivative identity uniquely fixes the latent translation without a normalization on \(U_1\). Moreover, \(\widehat q_x(u)=\widehat f_x(u)G_x(u,0)/F_x(u,0)\). Compact support makes both recovered transforms entire, so the local formulas determine \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) globally even when either error transform has an open zero set away from zero.
proposed.justification: It makes the causal ratio a functional of the observed marked replicate law without symmetry or global nonvanishing, over an explicitly inhabited class.
proposed.gap: Theorem 1 of Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy gives the probability-channel cocycle; it does not state the outcome-weighted signed channel or its compatibility with the recovered probability channel.
proposed.consumer: It supplies the law-level target set for honest-band inversion in two-recall exposure studies.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof now cites the moment-derived protected neighborhood, replaces primitive boundedness by the structural implication lemma, and records the explicit nonvacuity certificate.

proposed.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{low}}\) exhibit constants \(\eta\in(0,1-2\alpha)\), \(\varepsilon_R\in(0,\min\{R_f,R_q\})\), and \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\), and construct \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\in\mathcal M\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), with fixed \(p_x\), fixed positive \(f_x\), and fixed nonidentical asymmetric laws of \(U_1,U_2\) shared across \(j\in\{0,1\}\) and across \(n\), such that only the Bernoulli conditional means \(b_{j,n,x}\) differ; \(1/4\le b_{j,n,x}(a)\le3/4\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\); \(\sup_x\|f_x\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_f-\varepsilon_R\) and \(\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\sup_x\|f_xb_{j,n,x}\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_q-\varepsilon_R\); \(\operatorname{TV}(((P_{0,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},((P_{1,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le\eta\); and \(\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^{\infty}(I)}\ge c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}\)?
proposed.justification: This fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus is the unresolved lower-bound headline. The moment restriction supplies the protected neighborhood, so the question isolates the genuinely new packet-construction, strict-interior, and contiguity obstructions.
proposed.gap: No comparator fixes the density and two nonidentical asymmetric error laws while producing a valid Bernoulli marked perturbation with \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) supremum separation and an explicit \(\eta<1-2\alpha\) product-experiment total-variation bound.
proposed.consumer: An affirmative construction would combine with the conditional all-honest-band testing reduction; it would yield a matching converse only after a future \(O(r_n)\) upper theorem is proved.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The question remains open exactly as directed, but its dependency on primitive bounded outcomes is replaced by the proved structural-response implication.

proposed.statement: For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\). On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) there is a tuple \(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), formed from outer Jackson spline approximants and finite atomic error approximants, such that \(\|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}\). For every realized sample, the profiled clipping rule gives \(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\) and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\).
proposed.justification: This lemma proves concentration, equicontinuous outer-sieve embedding, ADRF approximation, and universal clipping for honest coverage.
proposed.gap: Its event argument gives no numerical inverse modulus; qualitative contraction is supplied separately by the finite-sieve diameter lemma.
proposed.consumer: It supplies feasibility and simultaneous coverage for the explicit clipped band and its consistent strengthening.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Every use of outcome boundedness and the marked envelope is now discharged by the structural-response implication lemma.

proposed.statement: There is \(n_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class indices, such that for every \(n\ge n_0\) the deterministic construction \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\) yields jointly sample-and-index measurable finite endpoints with \(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\), \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\) almost surely under every \(P\in\mathcal M\). More explicitly, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}\ge1-\alpha\), and coverage holds on \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\). In particular, \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le2B_Y\).
proposed.justification: The deterministic profiling construction has jointly measurable finite endpoints, nonvacuous uniform simultaneous coverage, and universal clipping.
proposed.gap: This base theorem records honesty; the separate finite-sieve diameter theorem supplies qualitative shrinkage but no \(O(r_n)\) rate.
proposed.consumer: It is the coverage and measurability input for the finite-sieve honest consistent upper theorem.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem now records model-class nonemptiness and obtains causal-curve boundedness from the proved structural consequence rather than a deleted primitive assumption.

proposed.statement:
Under the relaxed outer-sieve construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\), for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(x\in\mathcal X\), and all sufficiently large \(n\), there are splines \(\widetilde f_{x,n}\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(\widetilde q_{x,n}\in\mathscr Q_n(\widetilde f_{x,n})\) such that
\[
 \|\widetilde f_{x,n}-f_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\le a_{f,n},
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde q_{x,n}-q_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\le a_{q,n}.
\]
With the true masses \((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\), their profiled ADRF satisfies
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\frac{\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}-\mu(a)
 \right|
 \le 2\kappa^{-1}(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n})
 \le b_{\mu,n}.
\]
proposed.justification: The Jackson approximants satisfy the original relaxed density and marked-envelope restrictions and the deterministic Sobolev-modulus inequalities.
proposed.gap: This is an approximation and feasibility result; it does not quantify inversion of empirical channel discrepancies.
proposed.consumer: It supplies a feasible near-truth tuple for uniform coverage and preserves nonemptiness after the equicontinuity refinement.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The pointwise marked envelope is now obtained from the proved structural-response implications, with no primitive bounded-outcome dependency.

proposed.statement:
There exists \(n_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class
indices, such that for every \(n\ge n_0\) the abstract exact-class band
\(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\) has jointly sample-and-index measurable finite
endpoints, belongs to \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and satisfies
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \{L_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)
 \text{ for every }a\in I\}\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad 0\le W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\le2B_Y.
\]
Moreover, with \(\omega_n\) from
\(\mathrm{lem{:}qualitative\text{-}exact\text{-}grid\text{-}diameter}\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}]
 \le \omega_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}=o(1).
\]
The construction is qualitative and noncomputational; no explicit rate,
\(O(r_n)\) conclusion, or minimax claim is asserted.
proposed.justification: The theorem supplies a nonvacuous same-assumption inferential improvement: a uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band whose maximal expected width vanishes uniformly.
proposed.gap: The result is abstract and qualitative because compactness gives no explicit inverse modulus for the blind marked channel.
proposed.consumer: It supports consistent whole-curve uncertainty quantification while leaving the sharp \(r_n\) upper and matching marked converse as a separate research program.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The former empty-model branch is removed; explicit nonemptiness and the derived marked-envelope property now support the exact-class projection and the nonvacuous uniform guarantee.

proposed.statement:
There exists \(n_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class indices, such that for every \(n\ge n_0\) the finite-dimensional, semi-infinite deterministic profiling construction \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\) yields a band \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\) with jointly sample-and-index measurable finite endpoints, simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\) almost surely. Moreover,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \le \widetilde\omega_n+2b_{\mu,n}
   +2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}=o(1).
\]
No finite decision algorithm is claimed. The conclusion is qualitative and gives neither an explicit rate, an \(O(r_n)\) bound, nor a minimax claim.
proposed.justification: The finite-dimensional, semi-infinite empirical-characteristic-function profiling band is nonvacuously uniformly honest and has uniformly vanishing expected maximal width under the same assumptions.
proposed.gap: The theorem proves \(o(1)\) but not \(O(r_n)\); tightness and the fixed-nuisance marked converse remain open.
proposed.consumer: It provides qualitative whole-curve uncertainty quantification while separating consistency from the unresolved sharp-rate program.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The nonempty-model lemma is now a direct dependency so the headline uniform band guarantee cannot be read as vacuous.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For fixed indices admitting strict Sobolev interior, construct one fixed positive density and fixed nonidentical asymmetric error pair together with Bernoulli marked perturbations satisfying the range and strict slack constraints, achieving \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) separation, and having product-experiment total variation below \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The new primitive compatibility makes the full model and exact projected class nonempty, but it does not guarantee the strict interior required by this lower experiment; in particular the Bernoulli floor forces \(R_q>1/(4\sqrt{2B_A})\), while the class assumes only \(R_q>0\). Even in a strict-interior regime, the frozen primitives do not supply a moment-annihilating packet that simultaneously preserves the Bernoulli range and Sobolev slack or a weighted chi-square/Hellinger lower-envelope argument converting factorial Fourier attenuation into the required product total-variation bound.
open_obligations.attempted: The moment condition was used to obtain the protected neighborhood \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\), \(c_*=1/2\), and the new explicit reference law supplies fixed nonidentical asymmetric errors and a positive density. Moment annihilation was then carried through the marked-channel factorization to a factorial transform bound. These steps do not construct the required packet or control product Hellinger distance.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The moment condition supplies the protected neighborhood: by \(\mathrm{lem{:}moment\text{-}derived\text{-}local\text{-}modulus}\), every admissible error law satisfies
\[
 |\phi_Q(t)|\ge1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e},
 \quad
 \inf_{|t|\le\nu_*}|\phi_Q(t)|\ge c_*,
 \quad
 \nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1},\quad c_*=\frac12.
\]
Thus no separate spectral-modulus restriction is needed.  The new compatibility condition and \(\mathrm{lem{:}model\text{-}class\text{-}nonempty}\) provide a fixed positive density and fixed nonidentical asymmetric errors in an inhabited full model.  They do not, however, guarantee the strict interior required by the lower experiment.  Indeed, if \(b(a)\ge1/4\) and \(f\) is any density supported on \(\mathcal A\), then Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(1=\int_{\mathcal A}f\le\sqrt{2B_A}\|f\|_2\), and hence
\[
 \|fb\|_{H^\beta}\ge\|fb\|_2
 \ge\frac14\|f\|_2
 \ge\frac{1}{4\sqrt{2B_A}}.
\]
Consequently the requested inequality \(\|fb\|_{H^\beta}\le R_q-\varepsilon_R\) requires \(R_q>1/(4\sqrt{2B_A})\), whereas primitive compatibility assumes only \(R_q>0\).

Conditional on compatible strict-interior fixed nuisances, moment annihilation gives analytic attenuation.  Put \(h_n=f(b_{1,n}-b_{0,n})\), and suppose that
\[
 \int_{\mathcal A}a^kh_n(a)\,da=0,
 \quad 0\le k<K_n.
\]
For \(|u|\le\Omega\), Taylor's formula, \(|a|\le B_A\), and the cancellations yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat h_n(u)|
 &=\left|\int_{\mathcal A}
 \left(e^{iua}-\sum_{k=0}^{K_n-1}\frac{(iua)^k}{k!}\right)
 h_n(a)\,da\right|\\
 &\le\|h_n\|_1e^{B_A\Omega}
       \frac{(B_A\Omega)^{K_n}}{K_n!}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The marked-channel factorization makes the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the observed marked perturbation equal to
\[
 \widehat h_n(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
\]
For fixed error transforms supported in bounded frequency intervals, this transform is confined to a fixed square and inherits the factorial bound.  What remains unproved is a packet that simultaneously preserves the Bernoulli range and strict Sobolev slack, attains \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) supremum separation, and admits a weighted chi-square or Hellinger inequality strong enough to imply the required product-experiment total-variation bound.

prose_updates.tldr: The headline is statistical inference for a causal ADRF over an explicitly inhabited fixed class. A smooth reference-density/product-law construction proves that the model is nonempty, while the retained structural response surface derives both conditional unconfoundedness and bounded outcomes. Analytic cocycle identification enables the focal finite-dimensional, semi-infinite deterministic constrained-sieve band, which is uniformly honest, clipped to \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), and has uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. A parallel abstract exact-class band has the same qualitative consistency conclusion. sampling_model.design: The data are an i.i.d. sample of marked blind two-replicate observations \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i,S_{i1},S_{i2})\). Identification is an enabling step; the focal object is a uniformly honest simultaneous whole-curve band over a fixed identified and explicitly inhabited class.
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units have nonempty finite-stratum \(X_i\), compact latent dose \(A_i\), and potential-outcome schedules generated simultaneously by one jointly measurable response surface \(Y_i(a)=h(a,X_i,V_i)\), with \(V_i\perp A_i\mid X_i\). The surface range \([-B_Y,B_Y]\) implies a common-event schedule bound, observed-outcome boundedness by consistency, and conditional unconfoundedness; these are derived rather than separate primitive assumptions.
sampling_model.treatment: The replicates satisfy \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\). The errors are independent, need not be identically distributed or symmetric, may have open spectral zero sets, obey a fixed \(q_e>1\) moment radius, and use only \(E[U_2]=0\) to fix location. Their protected near-zero modulus is derived from the moment bound.
sampling_model.overlap: The target interval is a nondegenerate compact subset of \(\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)\), and \(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(a\in I\). Primitive compatibility requires \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\), \(R_f\ge R_{f,0}\), and \(0<p_{\min}\le|\mathcal X|^{-1}\), which permits the explicit reference-density witness.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-dimensional, semi-infinite deterministic profiling construction uses relaxed order-\(d\) B-spline families for \(f_x,q_x\), deterministic Sobolev-modulus inequalities, finite atomic characteristic-function families, and mass and channel confidence restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\). The continuum inequalities are imposed exactly, so no finite decision algorithm or certified numerical approximation is claimed. A parallel abstract construction profiles the exact compact projected class \(\mathscr K\).
sampling_model.tails: The structural response range implies \(|Y(a)|\le B_Y\) on one common event and hence \(|Y|\le B_Y\) by consistency. Each measurement error has a fixed \(q_e>1\) absolute-moment bound \(M_e\).

prose_updates.related_work: The organizing cluster is statistical inference rather than exact identification. Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle and compact-support density analysis that inform this paper; the present normalized scalar probability submodel is contained in their signal-identification setting but is stricter because it also fixes an error moment radius and centers \(U_2\). Their rate and minimax theorems concern \(L^2\) density risk under additional conditions and do not imply an ADRF supremum-band rate. Huang and Zhang study the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF with an everywhere-nonzero known error transform. Kato and Sasaki study deconvolution bands with auxiliary-error or conventional spectral information, Kato, Sasaki, and Ura study Kotlarski-based inference, and Babii studies honest diameter for fixed linear inverse operators. Hoffmann--Nickl and Bull concern adaptive direct-model bands, whereas this paper fixes \(\beta,R_f,R_q\) and claims no adaptation. Andrews and Mikusheva analyze nearly unidentified sequences; the present fixed compatible class obtains only qualitative contraction and does not cover drifting weak-identification regimes. Low supplies a testing-to-expected-length reduction only after a marked modulus is constructed. The explicit reference law repairs nonvacuity but does not supply that missing quantitative inverse or fixed-nuisance Bernoulli converse.
prose_updates.interpretation: The two observed channels identify \(f_x\) and \(q_x\), and therefore the continuous regression quotient \(q_x/f_x\). The structural response representation itself implies conditional unconfoundedness and a common-event bound on the potential-outcome schedule; positivity and causal-mean continuity then support the pointwise causal interpretation on \(I\). The normalized bump and asymmetric two-point error construction show that these conclusions are not artifacts of an empty class. The Melaku--Shi two-recall diet--mortality analysis remains motivation only; coverage applies to it only if its data-generating law satisfies the stated compatibility, support, overlap, structural-response, moment, and smoothness conditions.
